# Yautja
Few humans know they exist, and fewer live to talk about it. The [bold]Yautja[/bold] are an ancient, technologically advanced warrior species that has stalked the worlds of the near galaxy for thousands of years, hunting whatever offers a worthy fight.
## History - For ages the Yautja clans roamed their homeworld as nomads, following the herds they hunted. Clans rarely met, and when they did it was usually violent, so their technology barely advanced. - Then an asteroid struck the homeworld, scorching it into a desert. Whole clans and most of their prey died. The survivors had to cooperate or go extinct, and elected their wisest to lead them: the beginning of the [bold]Council of Ancients[/bold]. - The Council strictly controlled what, where and when the clans could hunt, so the little prey left wouldn't be wiped out. It merged the clans' scattered beliefs into one faith, and split society into a ruling warrior caste and a worker caste of craftsmen and scientists. - Over many thousands of years the clans rebuilt, advancing from bronze to the atomic age and on into space. The Council's decrees grew into a code of [bold]honor[/bold] that governs every part of their lives, from trade to how a proper hunt is carried out. - Reaching the stars, they found other life, and came to see the galaxy as theirs by divine right. Worthy prey was taken from its homeworlds and placed on reserves to be hunted, with care taken not to wreck the ecosystems that bred it. Many clans now live aboard great ships, nomads once more among the stars. - For more than a thousand years they have settled into a slow routine of hunting the worlds of their domain, more for pride and sport than for need.
## Faith - The clans worship the twin gods [bold]Nytara[/bold] and [bold]N'ithya[/bold], the two suns of their homeworld. In their legend, the gods slew a stone titan, [bold]Ger'Cetanun[/bold], whose shattered body became the planet's ring, and then created the Yautja from their own blood as warriors to stand against his promised return. - That vengeance came as [bold]Cetanu[/bold], the black death, who nearly destroyed their world. The Yautja survived and vowed to defeat him. Cetanu is now worshipped as the god of death and the ultimate foe every warrior strives to face. - Surviving Cetanu convinced them that the gods had made them perfect. Imperfection is not tolerated: dishonorable Yautja are exiled or executed, and for the very worst crimes an entire clan may be wiped out.
## Biology - Warm-blooded reptilian bipeds, 6 to 8 feet tall and around 500 pounds, with little difference between males and females. - They can live over 2,000 years, though their brutal lives mean most die between 800 and 1,000. - Pups are born after a three-year pregnancy, sealed in a hard sac they must break out of themselves. Those that can't are left to die as imperfect. - Strictly carnivorous; they can't digest plants at all. - Huge hearts give off enormous body heat, shed through the dreadlock-like tentacles on their heads. Cutting them off is a death sentence. - Four mandibles frame their mouths, and their language is made of clicks and rattles. They see in the infrared, are strong enough to tear bone from a body, and can leap three times their own height.
## The Clans From highest to lowest: - [bold]Council of Ancients[/bold]: ancient clan leaders chosen by the council itself. An Ancient's word is law. - [bold]Clan Leaders[/bold]: absolute authority over their clan, holding the position until they die in combat. - [bold]Elders[/bold]: masters of their skills, teachers of the young and leaders of hunts. - [bold]Elites[/bold]: blooded Yautja of great renown. They take on roles such as [bold]Enforcer[/bold], who punish breaches of the honor code; [bold]Hound Master[/bold], who handle the vicious hell-hounds; [bold]Shaman[/bold], who keep the temples and rituals; and others. - [bold]Blooded[/bold]: warriors who have passed their clan's rite of passage and earned the right to hunt. - [bold]Young Bloods[/bold]: those chosen to attempt the rite. Not all survive, and those who fail but live are expected to take their own lives. - [bold]Craft Masters[/bold]: the finest of the worker caste, one per craft in each clan: smiths, architects, shipwrights and creators. - [bold]Unblooded[/bold], those never chosen, do humble work under taskmasters, and [bold]slaves[/bold] sit at the very bottom.
## The Military Caste Most Yautja hunt for honor and sport. The [bold]Military Caste[/bold], or soldier caste, is called on when the species goes to war. Its soldiers and enforcers answer to the Ancients and the Elder Overseer, and they are not there for honor or entertainment: they are there to finish the job, with extreme prejudice. They carry the species' most advanced and destructive weapons, the kind an ordinary Yautja would consider dishonorable to use, which makes them far better equipped and far deadlier than their hunting kin.
